rules.statement: Tabs switch views of one object; if each view has its own URL, history and permissions, it is navigation and belongs in the sidebar.
The tab list is one tab stop with roving focus: arrows move, Home and End jump, and the panel is associated with its tab through aria-controls and aria-labelledby.
The active tab is reflected in the URL fragment or query so a reload and a shared link open the same view; changing tabs never pushes history per keystroke.
Each panel owns its loading, empty and error states; a failing panel never blanks the strip, and the tab label carries a small status dot with a text equivalent.
More than six tabs means the information architecture is wrong; if the strip must scroll it does so with visible affordances and keyboard access, never by clipping.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: each panel owns its request; a panel that finishes loading after the reader switched away is kept for its tab and never painted over the visible one

motion.motion: the indicator slides to the new tab over 160ms
motion.reducedMotion: the indicator appears on the new tab instantly

motion.motion: the panel dims over 120ms and keeps its height

motion.reducedMotion: the panel appears instantly and is announced

motion.motion: an inline error fills the panel over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the error appears instantly inside the same height

motion.motion: the panel returns to its pending state over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the panel returns to pending instantly

motion.motion: the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Let a reader switch between views of the same object without losing the tab they were on, and without the strip pretending to be navigation.
useCases: switch between Overview, Activity and Settings of one record
compare two views of the same data
reload and land on the same tab
nicheDifferences: Tabs are the cheapest information architecture and the most expensive when misused
Every tab must earn its place, because a hidden view is a view nobody visits
inputs: the number of views of this object and their independent states
whether the selection must be linkable
the longest tab label including translation
anatomy: a tab list with a moving indicator
per-panel loading, empty and error states
a status dot with a text equivalent
styling: the indicator animates position, not width, at 160ms
labels stay on one line with 16 px horizontal padding
the active label gains weight, not only a colour
a11y: role=tablist/tab/tabpanel with correct aria-selected and aria-controls
arrow keys move, Home and End jump, and focus follows selection
the panel is labelled by its tab
status dots are exposed as text, not colour
responsive: the strip scrolls inside its own container under 640 px with fading edges
labels do not truncate; they wrap to a second line before they clip
panels keep their height while loading to prevent jumps
copy: tab labels are nouns the reader would use, not internal module names
a failed panel says which panel failed and offers retry
an empty panel says what would appear here
alternatives: an anchored section list when the views are long and sequential
a sidebar when each view deserves its own URL
a split view when two panels are compared side by side
acceptance: the tab list is a single tab stop with arrow-key movement
the selected tab is reflected in the URL and survives reload
a failing panel never blanks the strip and offers retry
status is conveyed as text as well as a dot
the strip never clips; it scrolls or wraps
failureCases: each tab is a separate link and the browser history fills with duplicates
arrow keys move focus without selecting, and the panel never updates
a loading panel collapses and the page jumps
the sixth tab is invisible with no affordance

refused.reason: an unavailable tab is hidden or explained, not rendered as a dead tab stop
a segmented control with a dead segment is a lie about the choice set
